key_insight: ATLAS alternates between proposing mechanistic hypotheses and choosing experiments that best distinguish them, enabling active discovery of interpretable behavioral models.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a sample-efficient way to automate experiment design for model discovery, which could reduce data collection cost in scientific and cognitive-engineering applications.
method: Builds a diverse ensemble of sparse neural hypotheses (Disentangled RNNs).
Selects new experiments that maximally separate competing hypotheses.
Iterates hypothesis generation and experiment design to recover underlying reinforcement learning agents from bandit-task behavior.
evidence_signal: In silico evaluations show ATLAS improves sample efficiency by 5–10× over random experimentation across behavioral, structural, and computational similarity metrics, and it also matches expert-designed experiments.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated in simulated bandit tasks, so generalization to noisier real-world settings and more complex experimental domains remains to be validated.
paper_title: ATLAS: Active Theory Learning for Automated Science
